title_en: Bank of China Co., Ltd., Shantou Branch v. Guangdong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Shaoguan Branch and Third Party: Zhuhai Special Economic Zone Anran Industrial (Group) Company — dispute over subrogation
ruling_gist_en: Article 11 of Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: 'A creditor's subrogation action under Article 73 of the Contract Law shall satisfy the following conditions: (1) the creditor's claim against the debtor is lawful; (2) the debtor is delaying the exercise of its due claim, causing damage to the creditor; (3) the debtor's claim has become due; (4) the debtor's claim is not one exclusively belonging to the debtor itself.' Accordingly, a creditor's subrogation action requires the establishment of both the principal claim and the secondary claim. The establishment of a claim means not only that the content of the claim does not violate laws and regulations, but also that the amount of the claim must be determined. The determination of the claim amount may be reflected by the debtor or secondary debtor's recognition of the claim, or may be confirmed by a judgment of the people's court or an award of an arbitration institution.

full_text_en:
Bank of China Limited, Shantou Branch v. Guangdong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Shaoguan Branch, and third party Zhuhai Special Economic Zone Anran Industry (Group) Company — subrogation dispute

【Ruling Summary】

I. Article 11 of Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A subrogation action brought by a creditor in accordance with Article 73 of the Contract Law shall satisfy the following conditions: (1) the creditor's claim against the debtor is lawful; (2) the debtor is dilatory in exercising its matured claim against the sub-debtor, thereby causing harm to the creditor; (3) the debtor's claim has matured; (4) the debtor's claim is not one that is personal to the debtor." Accordingly, a creditor's filing of a subrogation action is conditioned upon the existence of the principal claim and the secondary claim. The existence of a claim means not only that the content of the claim does not violate laws or regulations, but also that the amount of the claim is determined. The determination of the amount of a claim may be evidenced by the debtor's or sub-debtor's acknowledgment of the claim, or may be confirmed by a judgment of the people's court or an award of an arbitration institution.

II. In accordance with Article 18 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues concerning the Application of the Statute of Limitations System in the Trial of Civil Cases, when a creditor files a subrogation action, it shall be deemed that the statute of limitations is interrupted with respect to both the creditor's claim and the debtor's claim.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 7

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Bank of China Limited, Shantou Branch. Address: No. 98 Jinsha Road, Shantou City, Guangdong Province.
Responsible Person: Yu Weichi, President of the Branch.
Authorized Agents: Wang Feng, lawyer of Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.
Authorized Agents: Li Boya, lawyer of Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Guangdong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Shaoguan Branch. Address: Building 41, Huimin South Road, Shaoguan City, Guangdong Province.
Responsible Person: Su Yang, President of the Branch.
Authorized Agents: Wang Dachao, lawyer of Guangdong Jingluefudian Law Firm.
Authorized Agents: Yuan Yongjun, lawyer of Guangdong Jingluefudian Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Zhuhai Special Economic Zone Anran Industry (Group) Company. Address: Room 802, Building 6, Yingbin Square, Yingbin Avenue, Gongbei, Zhuhai City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Liu Yifeng, General Manager of the Company.

In the case of subrogation dispute between the applicant for retrial Bank of China Limited, Shantou Branch (hereinafter referred to as Bank of China Shantou Branch) and the respondent Guangdong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Shaoguan Branch (formerly known as Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch, hereinafter referred to as GDB Shaoguan Branch) and the third party at first instance Zhuhai Special Economic Zone Anran Industry (Group) Company (hereinafter referred to as Anran Company), the applicant for retrial was dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2008) Yue Gao Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 5 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court and applied to this Court for retrial. This Court, by civil ruling (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 664 dated September 26, 2010, decided to retry this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Wang Xiansen serving as presiding judge, Judges Yin Yuan and Acting Judge Zeng Hongwei participating in the trial, and Court Clerk Zheng Qi'er serving as recorder. The trial of this case is now concluded.

The following facts were found at first instance by the Shaoguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province:

Based on the facts found in the civil judgment (2001) Yue Gao Fa Jing Yi Zhong Zi No. 172 of the Guangdong High People's Court, on August 17, 1995, Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as GDB Qujiang Sub-branch) and Bank of China Nan'ao Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as BOC Nan'ao Sub-branch) entered into a Loan Agreement numbered 95-08-001, which provided: The parties, in accordance with the principle of mutual benefit and equality, mutually agreed that GDB Qujiang Sub-branch would lend RMB 35 million to BOC Nan'ao Sub-branch as temporary revolving funds, with a term of 4 months (i.e., from August 17, 1995 to December 17, 1995), at a monthly interest rate of 11.55 per mill, and a daily penalty interest of 0.05% for overdue repayment. On the same day the contract was signed, BOC Nan'ao Sub-branch issued a Letter of Authorization to GDB Qujiang Sub-branch, stating: "To reduce intermediate steps, accelerate capital turnover, and improve the efficiency of capital use, we hereby authorize GDB Qujiang Sub-branch to transfer the funds of RMB 35 million lent to us into the account opened by our subordinate Nan'ao Jinzhu Industrial Development General Company (hereinafter referred to as Jinzhu Company) at GDB Shaoguan Branch, account number 605-2222-006-47. We acknowledge the funds lent by GDB Qujiang Sub-branch (loan agreement number 95-08-001)." Accordingly, GDB Qujiang Sub-branch transferred RMB 35 million into the account of Jinzhu Company as designated by BOC Nan'ao Sub-branch. On the same day, Jinzhu Company used a cashier's check to transfer RMB 623,000 from that account to GDB Qujiang Sub-branch, transferred RMB 6.733 million to the account of Jinzhu Company at BOC Nan'ao Sub-branch, and transferred RMB 27.644 million to the account of Anran Company at GDB Shaoguan Branch. Anran Company, on the same day, transferred RMB 15 million to the Real Estate Department of GDB Qujiang Sub-branch, with the purpose of the remittance recorded on the bank transfer voucher as "Purchase of land in Hengqin Island."

During 1992, GDB Qujiang Sub-branch had jointly developed a piece of barren land on Zhuhai's Hengqin Island with Hainan Beidao International Industrial Co., Ltd. Because Hainan Beidao International Industrial Co., Ltd. failed to pay funds to GDB Qujiang Sub-branch, on April 28, 1994, it notified the Administrative Committee of Zhuhai Hengqin Island Economic Development Zone, stating that due to its inability to raise sufficient funds for investment in the development of the land, it agreed that the right to use the land should belong to GDB Qujiang Sub-branch, and GDB Qujiang Sub-branch should handle the relevant procedures. On August 31, 1994, GDB Qujiang Sub-branch obtained the red-line boundary maps for three parcels of land with areas of 8,745.72 square meters, 12,000.005 square meters, and 5,599.95 square meters, respectively, and on November 25 and December 4 of the same year, it obtained the construction land planning permits for the above three parcels of land.

On February 28, 1994, GDB Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company entered into a Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement, which provided: GDB Qujiang Sub-branch agreed to transfer to Anran Company the development rights for 20,000 square meters of reclaimed land on Zhuhai Hengqin Island, and Anran Company was required to pay GDB Qujiang Sub-branch a total of RMB 33 million as transfer fees, interest, and service fees. The payment was to be made in three installments: the first installment of RMB 6 million as a deposit and RMB 16 million as land payment was due before May 10, 1994; the second installment of RMB 5 million was due before August 18, 1994; and the third installment of RMB 6 million was due before October 18, 1994. Upon full payment, GDB Qujiang Sub-branch would transfer all development and operation rights of the land to Anran Company. If Anran Company breached the agreement, it would be deemed to have voluntarily waived its right to receive the development rights, and GDB Qujiang Sub-branch had the right to reclaim the development rights and forfeit the deposit.

Separately, according to the civil judgment (2005) Zhu Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 35 of the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, it was determined that Anran Company should repay Bank of China Shantou Branch RMB 27.644 million in principal plus interest (calculated from August 18, 1995 until the date of full repayment at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period). This judgment has become legally effective. Anran Company has not yet performed its obligations under the judgment and its whereabouts are unknown.

On June 12, 1992, Anran Company was registered and established in Zhuhai City, leasing the third floor of the Nanyou Center Glass Building in Zhuhai as its office premises. It relocated its office in 1996 but did not go through the formalities for change of registration with the industry and commerce department. It still went through the annual inspection with the industry and commerce department on April 30, 1999.

On December 3, 2004, GDB Qujiang Sub-branch was dissolved, and its creditor's rights and debts were assumed by GDB Shaoguan Branch.

On January 26, 2007, Bank of China Shantou Branch filed a lawsuit with the Shaoguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, requesting: 1. confirmation that the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement entered into between GDB Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company was invalid; 2. an order that GDB Shaoguan Branch return RMB 15 million in land purchase funds, plus interest calculated at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, to be used to satisfy Anran Company's debts owed to Bank of China Shantou Branch; and 3. an order that GDB Shaoguan Branch bear the litigation costs of this case.

After trial, the Shaoguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province held that, according to Article 73 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, if a debtor is dilatory in exercising its matured claims and thereby causes harm to the creditor, the creditor may petition the people's court to exercise the debtor's claims in its own name by way of subrogation, unless the claims are personal to the debtor. Article 11 of Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: A creditor's filing of a subrogation action in accordance with Article 73 of the Contract Law shall satisfy the following conditions: (1) the creditor's claim against the debtor is lawful; (2) the debtor is dilatory in exercising its matured claim against the sub-debtor, thereby causing harm to the creditor; (3) the debtor's claim has matured; (4) the debtor's claim is not one that is personal to the debtor. Therefore, with respect to whether Bank of China Shantou Branch's exercise by subrogation in its own name of Anran Company's contractual claim against GDB Shaoguan Branch was in accordance with the law, the court held that it was an undisputed fact that Anran Company owed a debt to Bank of China Shantou Branch, as determined by the effective civil judgment (2005) Zhu Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 35 of the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province; and it was also a fact that Anran Company had paid RMB 15 million to the Real Estate Department of GDB Qujiang Sub-branch, with the purpose of purchasing land in Hengqin Island, as determined by the effective civil judgment (2001) Yue Gao Fa Jing Yi Zhong Zi No. 172 of the Guangdong High People's Court. However, it could not currently be determined whether GDB Shaoguan Branch owed a debt to Anran Company. This was because, although Anran Company had partially performed its payment obligations after signing the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement with GDB Shaoguan Branch on February 28, 1994, facts such as the validity of the agreement, whether it should be further performed, whether performance was possible, the reasons for non-performance, and the allocation of contractual liability had not yet been determined. It had also not been determined whether Anran Company held a matured claim against GDB Shaoguan Branch that was dilatory in being exercised. Therefore, there was insufficient evidence to find that, in this transfer relationship, GDB Shaoguan Branch was the debtor and Anran Company was the creditor. Accordingly, Bank of China Shantou Branch's exercise by subrogation in its own name of Anran Company's claim for repayment against GDB Shaoguan Branch did not satisfy the conditions for subrogation under the law. Its request for an order that GDB Shaoguan Branch return RMB 15 million in land purchase funds, plus interest at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, to be used to satisfy Anran Company's debts owed to Bank of China Shantou Branch, lacked factual and legal basis. In summary, in accordance with Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Actions, Article 73 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and items (2) and (3) of Article 11 of Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the court entered judgment: dismissing all claims of Bank of China Shantou Branch. The first-instance case acceptance fee was RMB 85,010, to be borne by Bank of China Shantou Branch.

Bank of China Shantou Branch, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment, appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court, arguing: (1) Anran Company was dilatory in exercising its matured claim against GDB Shaoguan Branch, thereby causing harm to Bank of China Shantou Branch's claim, and Bank of China Shantou Branch was entitled to exercise subrogation rights under the law. After Anran Company and GDB Qujiang Sub-branch entered into the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement, Anran Company paid RMB 15 million as "purchase of land in Hengqin Island" to GDB Qujiang Sub-branch on August 17, 1995. Thereafter, Anran Company did not continue to perform the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement and has not obtained the agreed land development rights to date. Its legal representative, Liu Yifeng, has been at large for many years due to suspected criminal activities. According to the contract terms, Anran Company should be deemed to have voluntarily waived its right to receive the development rights; therefore, the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement had in fact been dissolved. Moreover, the land development rights transferred under the contract pertained to the planning (red-line) requirements for state-owned land, and because the land was not transferred within the prescribed period, it had been re-planned for other uses. Furthermore, Anran Company and its legal representative were missing, making it impossible to continue performance of the contract. The Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement had completely lost any possibility of further performance. The court of first instance held that it had not been determined whether Anran Company held a matured claim against GDB Shaoguan Branch that was dilatory in being exercised, but this was precisely the fact that the court of first instance should have tried and made a determination on. The judgment of the court of first instance avoided these facts and dismissed Bank of China Shantou Branch's claims, which was contrary to both fact and law. (2) GDB Shaoguan Branch had not submitted evidence to rebut the existence of the matured claim asserted by Bank of China Shantou Branch. During the first-instance trial, aside from submitting a photocopy asserting that Anran Company made the payment on behalf of another person, GDB Shaoguan Branch only raised defenses regarding the statute of limitations, the validity of the contract, and the amount of liquidated damages, but did not deny the existence and maturity of the claim arising from the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement, nor the fact that Anran Company's dilatory exercise of its claim had caused harm to Bank of China Shantou Branch's claim. However, the court of first instance improperly exercised the right of defense on behalf of GDB Shaoguan Branch, which was clearly unfair. (3) The court of first instance committed errors in the application of law. The court of first instance's finding that "facts such as the validity of the agreement, whether it should be further performed, whether performance was possible, the reasons for non-performance, and the allocation of contractual liability had not yet been determined," and therefore "it did not satisfy the conditions for subrogation," was erroneous. First, whether the agreement should be further performed was clearly stipulated in the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement: if Anran Company failed to perform the contract, it would be deemed to have voluntarily waived its right to receive the development rights, and GDB Shaoguan Branch did not demand further performance during the litigation. Second, with respect to whether performance was possible and the reasons for non-performance, the facts had already led to a conclusion acknowledged by both parties: the land subject to the transferred development rights no longer existed, and Anran Company had been missing for over ten years, making further performance of the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement absolutely impossible. Third, the validity of the agreement and the liability for non-performance of the contract should have been determined by the court of first instance. The court of first instance's conclusion that the validity and liability were "not yet determined" failed to fulfill its adjudicative duties. During the second-instance court investigation, Bank of China Shantou Branch supplemented its grounds of appeal, arguing: (i) When GDB Qujiang Sub-branch entered into the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement, it had not obtained the right to use the land, and has not done so to date. Pursuant to the judicial interpretations of the Supreme People's Court, such agreements are generally deemed invalid. Therefore, the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement was void and should not be further performed. (ii) The Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement was an agreement that could not be further performed, as Anran Company had been dissolved and lost the capacity to perform the contract. (iii) After Anran Company was dissolved, it had been missing and had not asserted its own rights. GDB Shaoguan Branch, having received RMB 15 million without performing the contract with Anran Company, had obtained unjust enrichment and should not be protected. In conclusion, Bank of China Shantou Branch requested that the original judgment be set aside and that GDB Shaoguan Branch be ordered to return RMB 15 million in land purchase funds, plus interest at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, to be used to satisfy Anran Company's debts owed to Bank of China Shantou Branch, and that GDB Shaoguan Branch bear all litigation costs in this case.

The appellee GDB Shaoguan Branch responded in defense, arguing: (1) The RMB 15 million was remitted by Qujiang County Yintong Economic Development General Company through Anran Company to GDB Qujiang Sub-branch, and did not belong to Anran Company. (2) Bank of China Shantou Branch, as a third party, had no right to request a determination of the validity of the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement entered into between GDB Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company. (3) There was no clear creditor-debtor relationship between Anran Company and GDB Qujiang Sub-branch, and Bank of China Shantou Branch's exercise of subrogation rights did not satisfy the statutory conditions for subrogation. (4) Bank of China Shantou Branch's exercise of subrogation rights had exceeded the statute of limitations. The court of first instance made clear factual findings and correctly applied the law. GDB Shaoguan Branch requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

In response to GDB Shaoguan Branch's statute of limitations defense, Bank of China Shantou Branch argued: Bank of China Shantou Branch's exercise of subrogation rights had not exceeded the statute of limitations. After the civil judgment (2001) Yue Gao Fa Jing Yi Zhong Zi No. 172 became effective, Bank of China Shantou Branch had been continuously asserting its rights. On May 21, 2004, Bank of China Shantou Branch filed a lawsuit with the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, requesting confirmation that Bank of China Shantou Branch held a claim of RMB 27.644 million plus interest against Anran Company, and an order that Anran Company repay the debt of RMB 27.644 million plus interest. On November 4, 2004, the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province rendered a civil ruling (2004) Zhu Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 67, dismissing Bank of China Shantou Branch's lawsuit. After being dismissed, Bank of China Shantou Branch filed another lawsuit, and on December 30, 2005, the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province rendered a civil judgment (2005) Zhu Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 35, ordering Anran Company to repay Bank of China Shantou Branch RMB 27.644 million in principal plus interest. Additionally, on January 5, 2004, Bank of China Shantou Branch submitted to the Shantou People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province a "Report Requesting the Procuratorial Authority to Take Timely Measures to Recover Fraudulent Funds for Our Bank," requesting the seizure and recovery of Anran Company's illegal proceeds, i.e., the RMB 15 million "purchase of land in Hengqin Island" funds currently held by GDB Qujiang Sub-branch. Furthermore, although the Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement entered into between GDB Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company stipulated a performance period, after the stipulated performance period had expired, on August 17, 1995, Anran Company paid RMB 15 million to GDB Qujiang Sub-branch, which GDB Qujiang Sub-branch accepted without objection, indicating that the parties had effectively modified the performance period, rendering it a period without a fixed term. Since Anran Company's whereabouts were unknown, the statute of limitations should begin to run from October 2, 2005, when Anran Company was dissolved. Bank of China Shantou Branch submitted the civil ruling (2004) Zhu Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 67 and the "Report Requesting the Procuratorial Authority to Take Timely Measures to Recover Fraudulent Funds for Our Bank" as evidence.

Anran Company was duly summoned by the court of second instance but did not appear in court and did not submit any written defense opinion.

The Guangdong High People's Court confirmed the facts found by the trial court upon second instance. It further found: On August 21, 1996, Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch filed a lawsuit with the Shaoguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, requesting an order that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch repay the principal of RMB 30 million and part of the interest of the interbank borrowing, and bear liability for breach of contract and all litigation costs. The Guangdong High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2001) Yue Gao Fa Jing Yi Zhong Zi No. 172 on July 18, 2002, confirming that the "Interbank Borrowing Contract" was invalid, and ordering Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch to repay Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch RMB 28,990,075 plus interest. It also indicated that the rights, obligations and disputes concerning the RMB 15 million should be resolved through separate litigation between Anran Company and Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch, and the people's court would safeguard the litigation rights of the relevant parties. As Anran Company's whereabouts were unknown, the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province served the above civil judgment on Anran Company by public notice. The above civil judgment became legally effective on October 28, 2002.

On July 16, 2003, Anran Company underwent its last annual inspection. The current status of the enterprise is that its business license has been revoked. Its registered address on the business registration is Room 802, 6th Building, Yingbin Plaza, Yingbin Avenue, Gongbei, Zhuhai City.

The Guangdong High People's Court held in the second instance that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch filed the lawsuit claiming to confirm that the "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" entered into between Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company was invalid, and requesting to subrogatedly assert Anran Company's claim for the return of RMB 15 million in land purchase funds and interest from Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch. Since the validity of the "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" is related to whether Anran Company has a lawful claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch, this case may be identified as a subrogation dispute. Pursuant to Article 73 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 11 and 18 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (I), a creditor exercising the right of subrogation must satisfy the following conditions: (1) the creditor's claim against the debtor is lawful; (2) the debtor is negligent in exercising its matured claim against its debtor, causing damage to the creditor; (3) the debtor's claim has matured; (4) the debtor's claim is not one exclusively belonging to the debtor itself. The secondary debtor may assert its defenses against the debtor to the creditor. In this case, the fact that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch has a lawful and definite claim against Anran Company has been confirmed by the effective civil judgment (2005) Zhu Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 35 of the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province. Therefore, the focus of the dispute in this case is whether Anran Company has a matured and non-exclusive claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch; whether Anran Company is negligent in exercising its matured claim and has caused damage to Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch; and whether the defenses raised by Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch against Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch are valid.

Regarding the issue of whether Anran Company has a matured and non-exclusive claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch. The "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" entered into between Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company on February 28, 1994, based on its content, is a contract for the transfer of the right to use 20,000 square meters of reclaimed land on Hengqin Island, Zhuhai. However, when Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch signed the above "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement", it had not obtained the right to use the 20,000 square meters of reclaimed land on Hengqin Island, Zhuhai, and had not obtained such right of use or obtained the consent of the people's government with approval authority up to the time of this lawsuit. According to Article 55 of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, "A construction unit that obtains the right to use state-owned land through paid methods such as concession shall pay the land use concession fee and other land use paid fees and other expenses in accordance with the standards and methods prescribed by the State Council before it may use the land," and Article 9 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Contracts for State-owned Land Use Rights, "Where the transferor concludes a contract for the transfer of land use rights without obtaining the certificate of concession land use rights, and the transferor has obtained the certificate of concession land use rights or obtained the consent of the people's government with approval authority for the transfer before the lawsuit is filed, the contract shall be deemed valid." The "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" should be found invalid. The original trial judgment failed to make such a finding, which was improper. Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's claim in this regard has legal basis and is supported according to law. Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch, as an interested party, has the right to file a lawsuit to request the people's court to confirm that the above "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" between Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company is invalid. Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch's assertion that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch, as a third party, has no right to request confirmation of the validity of the "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" lacks basis and is not supported.

Pursuant to Article 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, after a contract is found invalid or revoked, property acquired under the contract shall be returned; where return is impossible or unnecessary, compensation shall be made. The party at fault shall compensate the other party for losses incurred; where both parties are at fault, they shall each bear corresponding liability. The invalidity of the "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" in this case was caused by the fault of both Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company, and they shall each bear corresponding liability. On August 17, 1995, Anran Company paid RMB 15 million to Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch by remittance, and the remittance voucher clearly recorded the purpose as "payment for land on Hengqin Island". Therefore, Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch should return the RMB 15 million "payment for land on Hengqin Island" paid by Anran Company, as well as the corresponding interest accrued during the period of possession of the funds, to Anran Company. Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch was liquidated on December 3, 2004, and its creditor's rights and debts were assumed by Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch. The above claim of Anran Company against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch is a monetary claim, which does not fall within the claims exclusively belonging to Anran Company itself as stipulated in Article 12 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (I). Therefore, the fact that Anran Company has a matured and non-exclusive claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch is sufficiently established. Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch's assertion that the RMB 15 million was entrusted by Qujiang County Yintong Economic Development Corporation to be transferred by Anran Company to Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch and did not belong to Anran Company is insufficiently supported and is not adopted.

Regarding the issue of whether Anran Company is negligent in exercising its matured claim and has caused damage to Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch. According to Article 13 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (I), "the debtor is negligent in exercising its matured claim, causing damage to the creditor" means that the debtor fails to perform its matured debt to the creditor and fails to assert its matured monetary claim against its debtor by way of litigation or arbitration, resulting in the creditor's matured claim not being realized. In this case, after Anran Company signed the "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" with Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch and paid the RMB 15 million "payment for land on Hengqin Island", it did not assert the RMB 15 million claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch through litigation or arbitration, and its whereabouts are unknown. Moreover, according to the finding of the effective civil judgment (2005) Zhu Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 35 of the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, Anran Company should return the loan principal of RMB 27,644,000 and pay corresponding interest to Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch. Anran Company has not performed the judgment obligation to date. Therefore, the fact that Anran Company is negligent in exercising its matured claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch, thereby damaging the interests of Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch, is sufficiently established.

Regarding the issue of whether Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch's defense that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's claim for subrogation has exceeded the statute of limitations is valid. On August 17, 1995, Anran Company paid RMB 15 million "payment for land on Hengqin Island" to the Real Estate Department of Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch. On August 21, 1996, the Shaoguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province accepted the dispute over the interbank borrowing contract between Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch and Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch, Jinzhu Company, and Anran Company. In that case, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch claimed that Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch had recovered RMB 15 million on the same day it lent out RMB 35 million, and requested that the RMB 15 million paid by Anran Company to the Real Estate Department of Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch be offset as a debt already repaid by Bank of China Nan'ao Sub-branch to Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch. According to Article 140 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, this lawsuit caused the statute of limitations for Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's claim for subrogation against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch to be interrupted. The civil judgment (2001) Yue Gao Fa Jing Yi Zhong Zi No. 172 rendered in that case clearly stated that the disputes concerning the rights and obligations of the RMB 15 million should be resolved through separate litigation between Anran Company and Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch, and the people's court would safeguard the litigation rights of the relevant parties. However, Anran Company's whereabouts were already unknown during the proceedings of that case and it did not participate. Therefore, from October 28, 2002, when the civil judgment (2001) Yue Gao Fa Jing Yi Zhong Zi No. 172 became legally effective, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch should have known that its rights were infringed, and the statute of limitations began to run anew. Pursuant to Articles 135 and 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, a party shall assert its claim to the people's court or a state arbitration body within two years from the date it knows or should know that its rights are infringed; otherwise, it will not be protected by the compulsory force of state law. Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch did not file the present lawsuit for subrogation with the original trial court until January 26, 2007, which already exceeded the two-year statute of limitations. Neither the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China nor the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (I) provides that a creditor's filing of a subrogation action must be preconditioned on a final adjudication confirming the principal claim. Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's argument that its lawsuit against Anran Company to confirm the principal claim constituted an interruption of the statute of limitations for its subrogation claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch lacks legal basis. Even if the "Report on Requesting the Procuratorial Authority to Take Timely Measures to Recover Defrauded Funds for Our Bank" submitted by Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch to the Shantou People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province on January 5, 2004, constituted an interruption of the statute of limitations for its subrogation claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch, by the time it filed the present subrogation lawsuit with the original trial court on January 26, 2007, it had also exceeded the two-year statute of limitations. Therefore, Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch's defense that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's claim for subrogation has exceeded the statute of limitations is valid and is supported.

In summary, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's claim for confirming the invalidity of the "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" between Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company is valid. However, its claim to subrogatedly assert Anran Company's claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch should not be supported by law as it has exceeded the statute of limitations. The original trial judgment found unclear facts and incorrectly applied the law, and should be reversed. Pursuant to Articles 135, 137, and 140 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 73 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 55 of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 11, 12, 13, and 18 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (I), Article 9 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Contracts for State-owned Land Use Rights, and Items (2) and (3) of Paragraph 1 of Article 153 and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows: 1. The civil judgment (2007) Shao Zhong Fa Min Yi Chu Zi No. 14 of the Shaoguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province is reversed; 2. The "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" entered into between the former Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company on February 28, 1994, is invalid; 3. The other claims of Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch are dismissed. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 85,010 shall be borne by Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch in the amount of RMB 42,505 and by Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch in the amount of RMB 42,505. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 85,010 shall be borne by Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch in the amount of RMB 42,505 and by Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch in the amount of RMB 42,505.

Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court, filed an application for retrial with this Court, arguing: (1) The principal claim of Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch against Anran Company has not exceeded the statute of limitations. According to the civil judgment (2005) Zhu Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 35 of the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, Anran Company is obliged to return RMB 27,644,000 and interest to Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch. This claim of Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch has not exceeded the statute of limitations. (2) The secondary claim of Anran Company against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch has also not exceeded the statute of limitations. The "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" stipulated that Anran Company would pay all amounts in full before August 18, 1994. However, Anran Company did not pay the RMB 15 million land purchase funds until August 1995, and Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch also accepted the payment. This should be regarded as a modification of the original contract into a contract without a definite performance period, and Anran Company has the right to assert its claim at any time. Furthermore, the second-instance judgment confirmed that the "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" was invalid, and the statute of limitations for the claim for return of property should be calculated from the date the contract was confirmed invalid. (3) The second-instance judgment's conclusion that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch exceeded the statute of limitations lacks legal basis. According to the principle of privity of contract, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch can only assert its claim against Anran Company. Only based on special legal provisions may the creditor Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch file a subrogation lawsuit against the secondary debtor Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch under specific circumstances. However, this does not mean that there is a direct legal relationship between Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch and Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch, and therefore there is no issue of statute of limitations. (4) Even if there is a statute of limitations for the subrogation action between Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch and Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's sending of a telegram in 2004 and its filing of a subrogation lawsuit with the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province in 2006 both served to interrupt the statute of limitations. Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's filing of this lawsuit has not exceeded the statute of limitations. In summary, the second-instance judgment misapplied the law. Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's subrogation lawsuit against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch has not exceeded the statute of limitations for either the principal claim or the secondary claim. It requests the reversal of the second-instance judgment and the issuance of a judgment ordering Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch to return the land purchase funds of RMB 15 million, plus interest at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, to be used to satisfy Anran Company's debts. Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch shall bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances.

The respondent Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch argued in its defense: (1) Whether the principal claim of Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch against Anran Company has exceeded the statute of limitations should be determined under the legal premise that the subrogation action is established. The subrogation action in this case is not established ab initio, so discussing whether the principal claim has exceeded the statute of limitations has no legal value. According to the principle of privity of contract, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch has no right to claim that the "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement" is invalid and demand the return of property. Under the provisions of China's contract law, a lawsuit contesting the validity of a contract is not the subject matter of a subrogation action. Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's abuse of the subrogation action seriously infringes on the contractual freedom and right of disposition of the parties to the contract and should be dismissed. (2) Regarding the "Cooperation Rights Transfer Agreement", there is no legal dispute or economic dispute between Anran Company and Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch, and there is no creditor-debtor relationship. There is no legal role of "secondary debtor" in this case. Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's assertion that the secondary claim of the debtor against the secondary debtor has not exceeded the statute of limitations lacks any factual basis and objective foundation, and completely fails to satisfy the legal constitutive elements of a subrogation action. (3) The right of subrogation provided for in China's contract law is the creditor's right to exercise on behalf of the debtor the claim that the debtor has against the secondary debtor. It is an external manifestation of the effect of the creditor's claim and a natural extension of the creditor's right. The secondary debtor's defenses against the debtor naturally apply to the creditor. There are disputes between the right to claim and the defense, and also between the right to claim and the counterclaim. Therefore, in essence, the subrogation action provided for in China's contract law belongs to the category of creditor's right to claim, which is a second-level creditor's right to claim distinct from the principal claim, and naturally the provisions on statute of limitations apply. Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's argument that the statute of limitations does not apply to subrogation actions lacks legal basis and is contrary to the statute of limitations system established by Chinese law. (4) Assuming that the subrogation action in this case is established, it has long exceeded the statute of limitations. According to the clarification and guidance of the Guangdong High People's Court's civil judgment (2001) Yue Gao Fa Jing Yi Zhong Zi No. 172, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch should have filed a subrogation action before October 28, 2004. Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's sending of a telegram to Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Branch on September 24, 2004, to assert its claim has no verifiable record and evidence, and does not comply with the statutory method of exercising the right of subrogation, so it cannot cause the interruption or suspension of the statute of limitations for the subrogation action. Its filing of a lawsuit against Anran Company for the repayment of the loan with the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province in 2005 has no legal logical relationship with the subrogation action and equally cannot cause the interruption or suspension of the statute of limitations for the subrogation action. Its filing of a subrogation action with the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province on September 20, 2006, not only exceeded the statute of limitations but was also filed in the wrong venue. Its filing of a subrogation action with the Shaoguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province on January 26, 2007, cannot change the objective fact that the statute of limitations had long expired. It requests that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's application for retrial be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

Upon retrial, this Court confirms the facts found by the Guangdong High People's Court in the second instance, and further finds: On January 5, 2004, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch sent to the Shantou People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province the "Report on Requesting the Procuratorial Authority to Take Timely Measures to Recover Defrauded Funds for Our Bank". The main content was that after the civil judgment (2001) Yue Gao Fa Jing Yi Zhong Zi No. 172 of the Guangdong High People's Court became effective, based on the provisions of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, our bank filed a lawsuit claiming the contractual right of subrogation. However, the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province considered that the case was not within its jurisdiction and informed our bank that we could sue Anran Company to determine the principal claim as the basis for the contractual right of subrogation. Based on the actual circumstances, our bank could only amend the complaint and first request confirmation of the principal claim against Anran Company. However, Anran Company's whereabouts are unknown, and the lawsuit may be protracted, making it impossible to effectively protect our bank's rights and interests. It requested the procuratorial authority to take timely and effective measures to seize and recover Anran Company's illegal gains, namely the RMB 15 million "payment for land on Hengqin Island" held by Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch.

On May 21, 2004, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch filed a lawsuit with the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, naming Anran Company as the defendant and the liquidation group of Jinzhu Company as the third party. On November 4 of the same year, due to the issue of Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's subject qualification, the court entered Civil Ruling (2004) Zhu Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 67, dismissing Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's lawsuit.

Opinion of the Court

In the course of the appellate proceedings of this case, in response to the claims filed by Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch, Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Sub-branch raised defenses including that the RMB 15 million payment did not belong to Anran Company, that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch had no right to request confirmation of the validity of the "Cooperative Rights Assignment Agreement" entered into between Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company, and that there was no clear creditor-debtor relationship between Anran Company and Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch. Based on the facts found in this case, the Guangdong High People's Court determined that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch, as an interested party, had the right to file a lawsuit requesting the court to confirm that the "Cooperative Rights Assignment Agreement" entered into between Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch and Anran Company was invalid; that Anran Company held a matured, non-personal claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Sub-branch; that Anran Company's failure to exercise its matured claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Sub-branch harmed the interests of Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch; and rendered judgment declaring the "Cooperative Rights Assignment Agreement" entered into between Anran Company and Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch invalid. In the retrial of this case, Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Sub-branch raised the same defenses. Regarding the fact of whether the RMB 15 million was a payment made by Anran Company to Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch, the Guangdong High People's Court's effective civil judgment (2001) Yue Gao Fa Jing Yi Zhong Zi No. 172 has already found and confirmed that the RMB 15 million payment made by Anran Company to Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch was an act of performance of the "Cooperative Rights Assignment Agreement" entered into by both parties. In this case, the determination of the validity of the "Cooperative Rights Assignment Agreement" not only concerns the confirmation of the creditor-debtor relationship between Anran Company and Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch, but also, since Anran Company cannot assert this right, it has a direct interest with Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch, which is a legitimate creditor of Anran Company, and directly affects whether the sub-debt claimed by Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch in the subrogation action actually exists. Therefore, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch, as the plaintiff in this case, filed a lawsuit requesting the court to confirm that the "Cooperative Rights Assignment Agreement" is invalid and to order Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Sub-branch to return the land purchase price of RMB 15 million and interest paid by Anran Company, which complies with Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 73 of the Contract Law of the PRC. The determination in the second-instance judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court that "the 'Cooperative Rights Assignment Agreement' is invalid; Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Sub-branch should return the principal and interest of the RMB 15 million land purchase price originally collected by the former Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch to Anran Company; and Anran Company's failure to exercise this matured claim harmed the interests of creditor Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch" is supported by sufficient evidence and the application of law is not improper. During the retrial of this case, the respondent Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Sub-branch did not provide new evidence to refute the above determination, so this Court confirms the above determination in the second-instance judgment.

The main focus of dispute in this retrial is whether the subrogation action filed by Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch in this case exceeded the statute of limitations period. Article 11 of this Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the PRC (I)" stipulates: For a creditor to file a subrogation action in accordance with Article 73 of the Contract Law, the following conditions must be met: (1) the creditor's claim against the debtor is lawful; (2) the debtor fails to exercise its matured claim, causing harm to the creditor; (3) the debtor's claim has matured; and (4) the debtor's claim is not a claim that is personal to the debtor. According to the above provisions, a creditor's filing of a subrogation action requires the establishment of both the principal claim and the sub-claim. The "establishment of a claim" not only means that the content of the claim does not violate laws or regulations, but also requires that the amount of the claim be determined. Such determination may be evidenced by the debtor's or sub-debtor's acknowledgment of the claim, or may be confirmed by a judgment of a people's court or an award of an arbitration institution. Therefore, before filing this subrogation action, creditor Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch confirmed its lawful claim against the debtor by filing a lawsuit with a people's court, indicating that it did not abandon its rights. Article 18 of this Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Statute of Limitations in the Trial of Civil Cases," issued on August 21, 2008 and effective on September 1 of the same year, stipulates: If a creditor files a subrogation action, it shall be deemed that the statute of limitations is interrupted for both the creditor's claim and the debtor's claim. This provision also indicates that a creditor's filing of a subrogation action simultaneously causes the interruption of the statute of limitations for two claims, i.e., the creditor's claim against the debtor and the debtor's claim against the sub-debtor, and both claims should be claims within the statute of limitations period protected by a people's court. Regarding the statute of limitations for the principal claim in this case, in the case of a dispute over a loan contract in which Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch sued Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch, Jinzhu Company, and Anran Company, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch argued that the RMB 15 million paid by Anran Company to Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch should be offset against the debt. The Guangdong High People's Court determined that "the rights, obligations, and disputes concerning the RMB 15 million should be resolved by Anran Company and Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch in a separate lawsuit." Since Anran Company's whereabouts were unknown and it did not participate in the proceedings of that case, and the court considered that the dispute over the RMB 15 million should be resolved separately, the creditor-debtor relationship and specific claim amounts between Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch and Anran Company, and between Anran Company and Guangdong Development Bank Qujiang Sub-branch, were not confirmed in case (2001) Yue Gao Fa Jing Yi Zhong Zi No. 172. After that judgment became effective, the statute of limitations period for the relevant claims enjoyed by Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch should have started anew, but Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's assertion of its rights was not limited to subrogation rights. In this case, after the Guangdong High People's Court's civil judgment (2001) Yue Gao Fa Jing Yi Zhong Zi No. 172 became legally effective on October 28, 2002, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch submitted a "Report on Requiring the Procuratorial Authority to Take Timely Measures to Recover Defrauded Funds for Our Bank" to the Shantou City People's Procuratorate, Guangdong Province on January 5, 2004, and on May 21, 2004, filed a lawsuit with the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court, Guangdong Province, asserting its claim against Anran Company. Although the lawsuit was dismissed by that court due to issues regarding its subject status, the act of asserting its civil claim still had the effect of interrupting the statute of limitations for that claim. Thereafter, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch again filed a lawsuit with the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court, Guangdong Province, which rendered civil judgment (2005) Zhu Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 35 on December 30, 2005, confirming that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch held a claim against Anran Company in the amount of RMB 27.644 million in principal and related interest. On January 26, 2007, Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch filed this lawsuit with the Shaoguan Intermediate People's Court, Guangdong Province. This claim did not exceed the statutory two-year statute of limitations period. Furthermore, the sub-claim in this case, i.e., Anran Company's matured claim against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Sub-branch, is a claim for restitution arising from the invalidity of the "Cooperative Rights Assignment Agreement." According to Article 58 of the Contract Law of the PRC, which provides that "after a contract is invalidated or rescinded, property acquired under the contract shall be returned" and "the party at fault shall compensate the other party for losses suffered," once the "Cooperative Rights Assignment Agreement" is confirmed invalid by law, Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Sub-branch is obligated to return to Anran Company the principal amount of RMB 15 million and interest of the land purchase price it collected. The two-year statute of limitations period for this claim (the sub-claim in this case) starts from the date when the contract was confirmed invalid by the second-instance judgment of this case. Creditor Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's assertion of this claim on behalf of Anran Company against Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Sub-branch did not exceed the statutory two-year statute of limitations period. The determination in the original trial judgment that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch's filing of this subrogation action exceeded the statute of limitations was insufficiently based and should be corrected.

In summary, neither the principal claim nor the sub-claim involved in this subrogation action exceeded the statutory statute of limitations period, and the creditor-debtor relationship is clear and the claim amounts are determined. Since Anran Company is unable to assert its matured claim, the ground for retrial of Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch that "Guangdong Development Bank Shaoguan Sub-branch should perform the obligation to pay RMB 15 million in debt to Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch on behalf of Anran Company" is established, and this Court supports it. When this payment obligation is actually performed, the total payment amount shall be limited to the total amount of the claim that Bank of China Shantou Sub-branch holds against Anran Company. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 73 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Articles 11, 19, and 20 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the PRC (I)," Article 18 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Statute of Limitations in the Trial of Civil Cases," and Item (2) of Paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court renders the following judgment:

1. Affirm items 1 and 2 of the main text of the civil judgment (2008) Yue Gao Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 5 of the Guangdong High People's Court;

2. Reverse item 3 of the main text of the said civil judgment;

3. Guangdong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Shaoguan Sub-branch shall pay to Bank of China Co., Ltd., Shantou Sub-branch the principal amount of RMB 15 million and interest (interest calculated at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, payable from August 18, 1995 until the date of actual payment). Upon performance of the above payment obligation, the corresponding amounts of the creditor-debtor relationship between Bank of China Co., Ltd., Shantou Sub-branch and Zhuhai Special Economic Zone Anran Industrial (Group) Company, and between Zhuhai Special Economic Zone Anran Industrial (Group) Company and Guangdong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Shaoguan Sub-branch, shall be extinguished.

The above payment obligation shall be performed within ten days from the date this judgment becomes effective. In case of delayed performance, the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

The court acceptance fees for the first and second instances of this case are RMB 85,010 each, totaling RMB 170,020, to be borne by Guangdong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Shaoguan Sub-branch.

This judgment is final.

Judge: Yin Yuan
